name: Koh Ker: Archaeological Site of Ancient Lingapura or Chok Gargyar
description: Deep in the jungle of northern Cambodia, about 120 km from Angkor, Koh Ker was briefly the Khmer Empire's sole capital from 928 to 944 CE. King Jayavarman IV filled it with around forty temples and a vast reservoir. Its showpiece is a 36-metre seven-tiered pyramid rising above the trees, while many more sanctuaries still lie hidden in the forest.
